releases.note: A worker delegated Notification Requests also owns the work their answers unblock: report it as waiting, never done, until that work is done. Name that work with `ask --resumes`. After a guidance change or compaction, load the skill again and run `notifai guidance`.
If `notifai guidance` reports that guidance changed while it printed, run it again before your next Notification Request.
An answer returns to its asking Agent Session. Do the work it unblocks there before reporting: a report sent in place of that work may never be read.
A delegated worker keeps its assignment until it does the work its answer unblocks, before reporting. Describe that work in `ask --resumes`; reporting the answer is not that work.
A worker delegated Notification Requests owns the work its answer unblocks. Keep the assignment waiting until that work is done, and name the work this Agent Session does in ask --resumes.

Use --choice-description when a choice label alone does not explain its effect, and --recommended <label> for the recommended choice. Keep recommendation markers out of labels. The CLI now converts a trailing (recommended) or [recommended] into recommendation metadata and refuses conflicting recommendations.
Cursor sends now use its native conversation identifier when available. Older Cursor shells remain detection-only; asynchronous questions and notes still require a proven continuation route.
Cursor can receive Session Notes through a held native Stop continuation. OpenClaw native Codex shells retain their OpenClaw session identity.
Cursor Session Presence ends when its native agent exits, even if an intermediate hook shell remains alive.
A new Cursor prompt fences the previous held Stop before it can deliver another note.
Notifai no longer runs git where no repository can be found, so a Mac without the developer tools no longer offers to install them when Notifai checks setup. Existing agent guidance is unchanged.

Setup reads more plainly. The computer-approval message an agent relays now tells the User to scan the QR code with their phone's camera, sign in with their email if asked, check the code and approve. Interactive `notifai init` asks about hooks, command approval and the skill only after the setup notification arrives. A Mac's default computer name drops `.local`, and a registered phone that cannot receive yet gets the one step it is missing. Existing agent guidance is unchanged.

Setup now gives agents scripts for every moment that needs the User. Harness setup and recovery opens with "What to tell the User": short, named lines for installing, approving this computer, getting the phone app, allowing notifications on iPhone and Android, the hooks choices, Codex `/hooks` approval, a new Claude Code session and finishing, plus one recovery line for each common failure. Read it before your first setup message to the User and say the script for the current moment as written. The Codex `/hooks` request reads more plainly.

Setup no longer needs a plan; delivering notifications does. An Account without a plan can approve this computer, install the phone app and wire its harnesses, so `notifai init` now asks for the app first and reports the plan as the last step, in place of the test notification, which it does not send without a plan. `send` and `ask` refused for that reason print one line with the stable code `no_active_plan`: "Notifai needs an active plan to deliver notifications. Choose one at <plans page>". The `no-plan` setup script now says the same. A running Notifai no longer treats a missing plan as a refused credential: it keeps the computer paired and resumes once a plan is active.

Getting the phone app no longer opens a page on the computer. Interactive `notifai init` shows a QR in the terminal that a phone's camera opens straight to the App Store (iPhone) or the free Android test sign-up, with one line saying to sign in with the same email and allow notifications. The devices gap's remedy and `notifai devices` name the same two links, and `init --json` adds them to the devices gap as `technical.install_urls`. Existing agent guidance is unchanged.

Every gap in `notifai init --json` now carries `message`: the exact line to send the User, written by the CLI for that gap. It covers approving this computer, getting the phone app, allowing notifications on iPhone and Android, a declined or expired approval, an unreachable service, an Account without a plan, Codex `/hooks` approval and an unconfirmed test notification; any other gap says what Notifai reported and what it asks for. States that need nothing from the User carry `null`. Harness setup and recovery now says: close a gap themselves when its remedy is a command they can run, otherwise send its `message` exactly as written, and keeps scripts only for the moments that are not gaps (installing, the approval link when the QR cannot be shown, the hooks choices, a new Claude Code session, finishing, and cloud or unknown computers). With an older Notifai that has no `message`, say what `remedy.summary` asks in plain words.

While an Account has no plan, `notifai init` counts a registered phone or desktop app that has notification permission as set up, so the plan is the one remaining step. A desktop app cannot keep its delivery stream open before a plan is active. Existing agent guidance is unchanged.

The setup notification is a confirmation, not a setup step. `notifai init --json` reports `ready: true` once this computer, the Project and a phone that can receive are set up, whether or not the app has confirmed the test notification. Until it confirms, the `proof` state is an optional gap with no `message`: it asks nothing of the User and never sets the exit code. Never wait for it or ask the User about it. Init sends it last, at most once per machine and phone, watches about 10 seconds for its receipt, and never re-sends it; a later run only reads whether it arrived. A test notification that cannot be sent, or whose delivery is rejected, is a real `proof` gap: its `message` asks the User to open the app so it can reconnect. Interactive `notifai init` asks about hooks, command approval and the skill once each, right after this computer is approved and before the phone step, the plan and the test notification. The `done` and `done-no-questions` scripts no longer say the app confirmed the test notification. An older Notifai can report `proof` as a gap and `ready: false` because of it alone; setup is done all the same.
Codex internal memory workspaces no longer activate Notifai. Requests from these folders are refused with codex_memory_workspace; normal Projects and other harnesses are unchanged.

Hook installation and discovery now follow shared configuration files in the selected harness home without replacing symlinks. Codex approval remains specific to the active home: open /hooks in a session using that same CODEX_HOME, even when its hook files are shared with another home. Existing approvals are never copied automatically.

A note or Answer Edit that an ended Agent Session, or one whose harness process is gone, still owed an acknowledgement now stays on this computer for 30 days and is then dropped without being acknowledged. An acknowledgement the service recorded after its session ended now clears that session's local obligation.

A Codex question card whose question or option is longer than a device question now opens normally: the devices get a shortened question and the Body carries the full wording. A Codex card or Claude Code picker that Notifai still cannot carry is refused with what to fix: fix that and open the card or picker again.

Native Codex cards stay usable when capability or answer-control probes fail, and queued device registration is explicitly unconfirmed. OpenCode forms outside device limits stay native; partial device replies preserve unanswered rows. Claude Code, OpenCode and Codex keep shortened choice labels distinct and map answers to the original options. Localized and punctuation-distinguished ask choices work without changing existing unambiguous IDs. Unsupported Node hooks and early-exiting OpenClaw hook children leave the harness running. Existing hand-back guards still prevent duplicate answers.

The skill description now explains notifications and questions through the CLI, with separate triggers for User responses, substantial work finishing or failing, and a change of Agent Session job. Recent User activity or no mention of Notifai still does not suppress these triggers. Ownership and first-use guidance instructions remain in the skill body and lifecycle context.

Setup is one command you rerun until it is done: `notifai init --json --wait 240` waits for each User step itself (approving this computer, the phone, notifications, the plan) and returns when it changes or the time is up. Send its top-level `message` whenever it is present (it is set only when new for this setup run), including alongside `waiting: true`, then rerun at once while `waiting: true`, and end your turn on `stopped: true` (30 minutes without progress, or 90 minutes after the approval began, with an "almost there" message that promises no test notification); never ask the User to tell you when a step is done. The only setup question is which agent apps to connect: without `--apps`, on a computer with no agent app connected yet, the first gap is `apps`, whose `message` is the question and whose `technical` lists `supported` apps (`id`, `name`) and the `detected` ids; ask it once, then rerun with `--apps <ids>` (or `detected`). For the chosen apps setup installs hooks, the skill (machine-wide unless `--skills-scope project`) and command approval for Claude Code and Codex without asking; command approval also covers rerunning `notifai init`. The older per-piece flags keep working, and an older CLI that rejects `--wait` or `--apps` is updated with `notifai update` or set up with the earlier loop. Setup opens the approval page in the browser (not over SSH or with `--no-open`), keeps the approval open with the same code while it waits (approval codes last 30 minutes), names the Account once connected, opens the browser's phone steps for an already connected computer, no longer blocks on notifications a phone has not allowed (the done message warns), and ends with a message naming the Account and what each connected app needs next. Messages are shorter and formatted. The test notification goes out once per computer and phone: not on a rerun, not while its delivery confirmation is awaited, and not when the browser's setup page already sent it; a send the phone's push service refused is retried once, after the phone reconnects. The apps answer is remembered, "none" (or `--no-hooks`) included, so the apps gap never returns. Codex's `/hooks` approval never stops setup: during `init` the `hooks-trust` state is an optional gap whose `message` is the done message's warning. After an approval on the page setup opened, the phone message says to follow that page; the store links stay for approvals with no page opened (SSH, `--no-open`, `--approval notification`, which no longer opens a page). A code that can no longer be kept open is replaced with "That code expired. New one: …" in a new tab, and the 90-minute stop now says "Tell me when you want to try again." `--wait` works only with `--json`. When Codex hooks need approval outside setup (`doctor`, a refused `ask`), the message again says to use the same `CODEX_HOME` and turn the hooks on if they are off.

Agent Sessions can discover names from exact T3 native-session mappings and Codex named-thread metadata when the title index has no entry. Generated fallbacks are checked during attendance and upgraded when a usable host name arrives and the service supports the guarded upgrade route. Existing explicit names, semantic names, and User renames stay authoritative. Keep passing the same concise --session-label on sends and asks; use session rename only when the job changes. Local session-filtered diagnostics now include name-resolution outcomes and sends without recording title text.

Setup messages now put one idea per paragraph: the approval code, the link to open and the next step each stand out, and links have names. Send each message exactly as written as your whole reply. Keep its words, line breaks, blank lines and Markdown, don't quote it or put it in a code block, and add nothing except its QR. The install line no longer asks the User to allow prompts, and no setup message asks the User to report a step. On a Mac, the done message ends with a link to the desktop app.

Codex hook approval is now worded for the Codex surface you run in: `/hooks` in the Codex CLI, the Review hooks icon in the message box of the ChatGPT desktop app and the Codex IDE extension, or both when Notifai can't tell. Never wait for that approval or ask the User to tell you when it's done: carry on, and end your reply with the reminder doctor or ask gives (`message`, or `user_action.message`) as written. When `ask` is refused with `codex_hook_approval_required`, nothing was registered: ask the question in the conversation instead and carry on. The apps question names Codex "Codex (CLI, IDE or ChatGPT app)"; elsewhere call it Codex.
The hub no longer resends an attendance exchange the service refused, so a resumed conversation can no longer keep it retrying about once a second. Existing agent guidance is unchanged.

The hub now recovers by itself when its attendance exchange stalls or fails on a local write (such as a full disk), and a Stop hook takes over answer delivery from a hub that stopped exchanging. Existing agent guidance is unchanged.

A Codex thread whose Notifai hooks were never approved in its Codex home (for example, an app that starts Codex with its own `CODEX_HOME`, one per account) now shows as running in the Notifai apps once it sends: its send tells the hub where it runs, and the hub attends it while a Codex process holds the thread. Until its hooks are approved in that home it takes no notes, and questions still need that approval. The first send from such a thread now prints one line asking the agent to end its reply with a reminder to approve the hooks; in an app that runs Codex in its own home, the reminder names that home's terminal command (`CODEX_HOME=<home> codex`, then `/hooks`). Nothing waits for the approval.

Notifai's Codex trust check now keys an unset `CODEX_HOME` by the plain `~/.codex` path, as Codex does, so a `~/.codex` that is a symlink no longer reports approved hooks as unapproved, and `doctor`, a refused `ask` and the send notice stop asking for an approval that was already given. Existing agent guidance is unchanged.

The reminder to approve Notifai's Codex hooks now gets the User there without a sign-in. When Codex runs under an app with no hook review of its own (such as T3 Code), it names a terminal command, `CODEX_HOME=<home> codex -c model_provider=ollama` for an account in its own home, and the **Trust all and continue** choice; on Windows the PowerShell line also clears `CODEX_HOME` afterwards. Hooks that are turned off still take `/hooks`. In an Orca chat it says to approve once in `~/.codex`, which Orca copies to its Codex accounts. `notifai init` and its done message give the same step. Carry on and end your reply with the reminder as written, as before.

Codex sessions keep the Notifai handlers they loaded when they started, even after an update adds or changes one and the User approves it. `notifai update --resume` no longer reports the update done for such a session: it names each handler the session lacks and says a new Codex session picks it up. `notifai doctor` names the same handlers and blocks only when a feature needs one (turn end, the tool boundary or question cards); otherwise keep working and tell the User. Codex records which handlers a session loaded when it starts, and new Codex installs no longer carry an `--integration-revision` argument; existing installs keep their approved commands unchanged, so nothing needs approval again. Doctor reads hook approval from Codex itself where it can. Other harnesses are unchanged.

New: `notifai doctor codex` helps the User approve Notifai's Codex hooks. Run in a terminal, it finds the Codex homes where Notifai's hooks wait (`~/.codex`, the shell's `CODEX_HOME`, and homes Notifai saw a Codex thread run in) and opens Codex's own hook review in each, with no sign-in where the home has none of its own; the User approves there and Notifai re-checks. Notifai never approves its hooks itself. Run by an agent it launches nothing and prints the command for the User. Where Codex runs under an app with no hook review of its own (T3 Code, Orca), the reminder, the setup warning and the done message now name `notifai doctor codex` instead of `CODEX_HOME=<home> codex -c model_provider=ollama`, on every platform. `doctor`, a refused `ask` and `hooks install` add it beside Review hooks and `/hooks`. Never run it for the User; carry on and end your reply with the reminder as written, as before.

The reminder to approve Notifai's Codex hooks, the setup warning and the done message now say "in a terminal on this machine" for every app that runs Codex without a hook review of its own; they no longer add a note naming one particular app. The step itself is unchanged: run `notifai doctor codex` and choose **Trust all and continue** (or type `/hooks` for hooks that are off). Carry on and end your reply with the reminder as written, as before.

Wording no longer calls the conversation with an agent "the terminal", since many agents run in desktop apps. A question answered in Claude Code's picker or Codex's own question card is recorded on the User's devices as "Answered in the agent session." instead of "Answered in the terminal."; `notifai ask` and `notifai send --reply` refusals with question notifications off, the `ask_notifications` and `ask_grace_seconds` setting descriptions, `notifai doctor`, `notifai init` and the interactive question settings now say the question stays in the conversation. The skill's setup, Claude Code, Codex and diagnostics references say the same. Separately, when a question Notifai retires ended unanswered (Esc or "Chat about this" on a Claude Code picker, or the Agent Session ending), the CLI now tells the service so, and the User's devices show it as expired instead of answered elsewhere; a service that predates this is closed as before. Agents run nothing new.

The `Heads up (source.session_label)` line, printed when an Agent Session sends before it is named, now says the User sees the session under its generated name, such as "Yellow Bear", until it is named. A question opened through a harness picker in an unnamed session no longer freezes that generated name, so the first name you pass, or a proven harness title, still replaces it once. Nothing else changes: keep passing a concise `--session-label` on every send and ask.

`notifai ask` now refuses, before registering anything, a form whose questions and choice labels do not fit one phone notification (about 4 KB, usually no more than 8 short questions; the Body and choice descriptions do not count). The refusal has code `question_too_large`, names the size, and says to split the questions into smaller forms or shorten question texts, choice labels, the title or the summary. Such a form used to register, then end `retired` in the background with no reason, and the User never saw it. `notifai status <question_id>` now says why a retired or withdrawn question ended: a `Reason:` line, and `end_reason` (with `end_detail` for a service refusal) in `--json`; a service refusal reads "refused by the service — the User never saw this question". The local log records each such end as `ask.retired` with its reason.

A Claude Code conversation that T3 Code stopped after it sat idle now continues by itself when an answer or note arrives for it: while T3 Code runs, Notifai sends its own T3 Code thread a Notifai wake through T3 Code's `t3` command, the conversation comes back in that thread, and the agent takes the answer from there. It never continues in another thread or app, and never starts T3 Code; while T3 Code is not running it waits for the User as before. `reopen.t3` (`when-running` by default, or `off`) is the new per-place setting, and doctor's `Reopen:` line names T3 Code threads. A Codex thread in T3 Code still waits for the User. Agents should not ask the User to resume such a conversation.

A question form's room in the phone notification now depends on the Project's real name and avatar instead of the longest ones a Project may have, so ordinary forms of up to 10 questions fit: `references/send-details.md` now says 10 questions of about 60 characters with two or three short choices usually fit, fewer when they are longer (it used to say usually no more than 8 short questions). `notifai ask` learns each Project's room from the service on every send in that Project; until then it sizes a form for the longest name and avatar, so a form near the limit can be refused in a Project the CLI has not sent in yet. The `question_too_large` refusal, its message and remedy are unchanged.

A Codex conversation in T3 Code that has stopped now continues by itself in its own T3 Code thread when an answer or note arrives, as a Claude Code one already did: while T3 Code runs, Notifai sends that thread a Notifai wake through T3 Code's `t3` command. Notifai finds the thread from T3 Code's own record when the hooks could not name it (a Codex thread runs on T3 Code's shared Codex server, whose environment names no thread), and accepts T3 Code's longer delegated-task thread ids. `reopen.t3` covers both. Agents should not ask the User to resume such a conversation.

Each question of a `notifai ask --form`/`--form-json` form can now carry an optional `"detail"`: short Markdown (at most 500 characters, no images) explaining why that question is asked and what rides on it. The User's devices show it under the question's text in a quieter style, and the question's `"title"` above it. The `questions` guidance now says to keep each question's text to the question and put its own reasoning in its `"detail"`, not in the text or the form's Body; the form's Body stays for context every question shares. A `"detail"` that is too long, empty or holds an image is refused with what to change. A question `"title"` longer than 40 characters still heads the terminal form, and the CLI notes that devices leave it out. Nothing else changes: single questions keep `--title`, the Summary and `--body`.

Notifai's hooks now have short names. Claude Code shows a hook's name while it runs. Codex shows the names in `/hooks` and the ChatGPT app's hook review for installs that carry no integration revision (fresh installs since 14.4.2-beta.4); Codex treats those renamed hooks as changed, so the User approves them once. Codex installs that carry a revision keep their approved hooks byte-for-byte and need no new approval. Grok, Cursor, OpenCode, OpenClaw and Hermes are unchanged. Nothing changes in what agents do.

A missing Agent Acknowledgement now holds the turn for at most three Stops in a row in every case. This includes a Stop that is already a continuation while another question still waits. After that the turn ends and the owed acknowledgement is dropped. What agents should do is unchanged: acknowledge an answer as soon as it arrives.

A long Claude Code picker, Codex card or OpenCode question now reaches devices as the question it asks: its last sentence ending in a question mark, else its closing whole sentences, never a fragment after an ellipsis. Its full wording goes into the Body with its lines kept and its bullet lines as a list, no longer as one bold paragraph. Only a question that was shortened or has notes appears in the Body. Nothing changes in what agents do: write the picker as usual, and the answer still maps back to the exact picker wording.

Agents can now make a plain folder a Project by name on this computer: `notifai project folder add <path> --name <name>`, with `list`, `rename` and `remove` (each takes `--json`). Outside a Git repository, a send or ask from that folder or any folder inside it then carries that Project. A Git repository inside the folder keeps its own Project, and an explicit, configured or `--projectless` choice still wins. Do it when the User asks; the folder's path never leaves the computer.
